narrative.overview:
Warm paper, black ink, and one living signature. The site is a deck of full-screen panels, each holding one idea: who Nathan is, where he has worked, what he has built, what he builds with, who he is outside work, and how to reach him. It is quiet on purpose, with wide margins, a single centred heading per panel and plenty of empty paper, so the two moments of colour carry the weight. The look follows brandondavid.dev, which Nathan chose as the reference, filled with his own, richer content.

The signature is the giant lowercase "sta monica" set in DM Serif Display along the bottom of the first screen. Its letters are filled with a WebGL liquid of navy, cobalt and violet with iridescent rims, which leans toward the pointer. Everything else stays typographic: Inter on paper, underlined ink links, hairline rows, small coloured dots for each employer. The only dark surface is the featured project card.

On laptops and desktops the panels behave like a deck that scrolls the way brandondavid.dev does. Each panel rests for a third of a screen of scrolling, then the next one slides up over it, following the wheel or trackpad one to one, while the one beneath blurs and fades away behind it. The deck stops wherever the scrolling stops, even halfway, with both panels in view. The keys, in-page links and the ⌘K menu glide a whole panel on a spring. On phones and tablets the same panels scroll normally and sharpen as they enter. Without JavaScript the page is a plain, complete scroll with ink letters.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground (#eeeee0) and near-black ink; no white surfaces.
One serif voice (DM Serif Display) for the wordmark and the closing line; Inter for everything else.
Colour lives in two places only: the liquid inside the wordmark and the saturated brand tiles of the tech marquee.
One idea per full-screen panel, headed by a casual sentence that ends in an ellipsis.
Motion is structural: the wordmark rises, panels slide over one another as you scroll while the covered one blurs away, tiles slide; nothing decorative.

rules.name: The Two Homes Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour appears in exactly two places: inside the wordmark (the liquid) and on the tech tiles. Tones elsewhere are dots and bullets, never fills, borders or text on paper.

rules.name: The Paper Wins Rule
rules.body: The liquid canvas sits over the ink letters with `mix-blend-mode: lighten`, and every colour it draws is clamped to at most (0.86, 0.86, 0.82), darker than the paper. Over paper the paper wins and over the ink the liquid shows. Never let a liquid colour exceed the paper, or the canvas's rectangle appears around the letters.

rules.name: The One Serif Voice Rule
rules.body: DM Serif Display appears only in the wordmark, the closing line, the 404 mark and the link preview. Never use it for headings, buttons or UI.

rules.name: The Casual Heading Rule
rules.body: Panel headings are lowercase-style sentences in Inter regular, centred, ending in an ellipsis. No kicker, eyebrow or section number above them.

rules.name: The Medium Ink Rule
rules.body: Every Inter text runs at 500 (one `--weight-text` setting). Hierarchy comes from size and colour first; names step up to 600, the featured project name to 700, and numbers marked in the copy to 700. Never set Inter below 500, and never ask DM Serif Display for a weight it does not have (it stays at 400).

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Rows, tags, headings and links never cast shadows. If something needs separation on paper, use a hairline or the Pressed Paper fill.

dos: Do keep every panel on Warm Paper (#eeeee0). The paper is the brand.
Do put new colour only on the tech tiles or inside the wordmark (The Two Homes Rule).
Do head each panel with one casual, centred Inter sentence that ends in an ellipsis.
Do make anything new keyboard-reachable inside its panel; the deck follows focus.
Do keep numbers understated: bold weight inside running text, never big stat blocks.
Do give anything that must survive without JavaScript a native element (details/summary, plain links).
Do put hover-only effects inside `@media (hover: hover)`: on an iPhone a tap would leave them stuck on (a faded email, a grey row, a paused marquee).
Do keep photography personal and singular: one real photo print in About, never stock imagery or decorative pictures.
donts: Don't add white cards, glass panels or a background behind the whole page. The liquid lives only inside the wordmark.
Don't use DM Serif Display for headings, buttons or UI text (The One Serif Voice Rule).
Don't put kickers, eyebrows or section numbers above panel headings.
Don't add hero-metric blocks (big number, small label) for the resume figures.
Don't let any liquid colour reach the paper's lightness (The Paper Wins Rule).
Don't add a navigation bar or panel dots; the deck, the in-text links and ⌘K are the navigation.
